teach.ask: Gappu has a round leaf and wants to find its middle. How can he do it?
teach.praise: Fold, fold again, and the lines cross at the centre! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How many folds do I need?

revise.summary: A bangle, a coin and a wheel are circular. Fold a circle twice in different directions to find its centre.
focus: Draw a circle by tracing round things.
Find the centre by folding.
Spot circular objects and games played in a circle.
remember: Two folds cross at the centre.
The centre is the same distance from every point on the circle.
traps: One fold is not enough to find the centre.
The centre is not on the edge.
A dice face is a square, not a circle.

topics.title: Comparing shapes and odd one out

learn.hook: Square, rectangle, triangle, circle. Which is the odd one out? There could be more than one answer!
points: Compare shapes by the number of sides and the kind of corners.
A square and a rectangle both have 4 sides and 4 square corners. A triangle has 3 sides.
In odd one out, each shape could be different for a reason: the circle has no corners; the triangle has 3 sides.
Always give a reason for your choice.
To find the largest rectangle, compare how much space each covers, for example by counting the squares inside.

example.q: Odd one out: square, rectangle, triangle. Give a reason.
steps: Square: 4 sides. Rectangle: 4 sides. Triangle: 3 sides.
example.answer: Triangle, because it has only 3 sides

learn.reallife: Sorting shapes is how shop owners arrange tiles, boxes and plates neatly.

quiz.q: How are a square and a rectangle ALIKE?
quiz.explain: Both have 4 sides and 4 square corners.

quiz.q: How is a triangle DIFFERENT from a square?
quiz.explain: A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.
steps: A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.
A square has 4 sides and 4 corners.
Answer: It has 3 sides instead of 4

quiz.q: Odd one out: circle, square, rectangle. Which is odd and why?
quiz.explain: The square and rectangle have corners. The circle has none.
steps: Count the corners: circle 0, square 4, rectangle 4.
The circle is different. It has no corners.
Answer: Circle: it has no corners

quiz.q: Odd one out: square, rectangle, pentagon. Which is odd and why?
quiz.explain: The square and the rectangle have 4 sides. The pentagon has 5.
steps: Count the sides: square 4, rectangle 4, pentagon 5.
quiz.mistake: Does not compare the number of sides

quiz.q: Which rectangle is the largest? A covers 6 squares, B covers 8, C covers 4.
quiz.explain: 8 squares is the most space.
steps: A covers 6 squares, B covers 8, C covers 4.

quiz.q: Rectangle A is 3 squares long and 2 wide. How many squares does it cover?
quiz.explain: 2 rows of 3 = 6 squares.
steps: The rectangle is 3 squares long and 2 squares wide.

quiz.q: Shape X has 4 equal sides and 4 square corners. Shape Y has 4 sides, opposite sides equal, and 4 square corners. Both are…
quiz.explain: X is a square, which is also a rectangle. Y is a rectangle.
steps: X has 4 equal sides and 4 square corners: a square.
Y has opposite sides equal and 4 square corners: a rectangle.
A square is a special rectangle, so both are rectangles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a square is not a rectangle

quiz.q: Odd one out: triangle, triangle, triangle, square. Why is square odd?
quiz.explain: The square has 4 sides and the rest have 3.
steps: Count the sides: triangle 3, triangle 3, triangle 3, square 4.
The square is the only one with 4 sides.

teach.ask: Gappu thinks the odd one out among circle, square and triangle can only be the circle. Is that right?
teach.praise: Oh! The triangle is odd too, because it has 3 sides. Each can be odd for a reason! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Can the triangle be the odd one out for some reason?

revise.summary: Compare shapes by the number of sides and the kind of corners. In odd one out, always give a reason.
focus: Say how shapes are alike and different.
Find the odd one out with a reason.
Compare rectangles by counting the squares they cover.
remember: Square and rectangle: 4 sides, 4 square corners. Triangle: 3 sides.
traps: Don't pick without a reason.
A square is also a rectangle.
Don't add length and width. Count the squares.

learn.hook: Two corners are given on dot paper. Where do the other two corners go?
points: To complete a rectangle with a gap, pick a piece that fills the gap exactly, with no overlap.
Game: your friend marks two opposite corners on dot paper. You draw the rectangle using them.
From opposite corners, go across from one and down from the other. Where they meet are the missing corners.
A shape can be drawn big or small, standing up or lying down. It is still the same kind of shape.

example.q: Opposite corners of a rectangle are at the top-left and bottom-right. Where are the other two?
steps: Top-right: same row as top-left, same column as bottom-right.
Bottom-left: same row as bottom-right, same column as top-left.

learn.reallife: Jigsaw puzzles and tiled floors need the right piece to fill each gap.

games.title: Gap and size facts
items: A small square drawn big is still a square.
Size does not change the shape.
A rectangle turned on its side becomes a triangle.
To fill a gap, the piece must match the gap exactly.
Two opposite corners are enough to draw a rectangle (with sides along the grid).
The other two corners are found from them.

items.text: Corners at (row 1, col 1) and (row 3, col 4). Missing: (row 1, col ___) and (row 3, col 1)
Gap is 2 squares long and 1 square wide. Fill with a piece of ___ squares
A big square is still a ___

quiz.q: A 3 by 2 rectangle has a gap of 2 squares in a row. Which piece fills it?
options: A piece of 2 squares in a row
quiz.explain: The piece must match the gap: 2 squares in a row.
steps: The gap is 2 squares in a row.
The piece must fill it exactly, with no overlap.
A 3-square piece is too big. A circle or triangle will not fit.
Answer: A piece of 2 squares in a row
quiz.mistake: Picks a piece that is too big

quiz.q: A rectangle covers 6 squares. 4 are filled. How many squares are in the gap?
steps: The rectangle covers 6 squares. 4 are filled.

quiz.q: On dot paper, a rectangle has corners at top-left and bottom-right. How many corners are missing?
quiz.explain: A rectangle has 4 corners. 2 are given, so 2 are missing.

quiz.q: Opposite corners are top-left and bottom-right. Which corner is in the SAME ROW as top-left?
quiz.explain: The top row has top-left and top-right.
steps: Top-left is in the top row.
The other corner in the top row is top-right.

quiz.q: Mira draws a tiny triangle and a huge triangle. What is the same about them?
quiz.explain: Size changes, but the shape's sides and corners stay the same.
steps: A tiny triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.
A huge triangle also has 3 sides and 3 corners.
Size changes, but the kind of shape stays the same.
Answer: Both have 3 sides and 3 corners

quiz.q: A rectangle is drawn standing up and the same one is drawn lying down. Are they the same shape?
quiz.explain: Turning does not change a shape.
steps: Standing up or lying down, the rectangle has the same sides and corners.
Turning does not change a shape.

quiz.q: A 4 by 2 rectangle has 8 squares. A piece of 3 squares fills part of a gap of 5. How many more squares needed?
Which piece would NOT fit a gap of 1 square?
quiz.explain: A 2-square piece is too big and would overlap.
steps: A 2-square piece is too big and would overlap.

teach.ask: Gappu's friend marked two opposite corners on dot paper. How can Gappu draw the rectangle?
teach.praise: Go across from one corner and down from the other. The meeting points are the missing corners! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How do I find the two missing corners?

revise.summary: To complete a rectangle, use a piece that fills the gap exactly. From two opposite corners we can find the missing two corners.
focus: Choose the piece that fills a gap exactly.
Find missing corners of a rectangle on dot paper.
Know that size and turning do not change a shape.
remember: A rectangle has 4 corners. 2 given → 2 missing.
Opposite corners top-left and bottom-right → missing top-right and bottom-left.
Gap squares = total squares − filled squares.
traps: A piece that is too big will overlap.
Don't mix up rows and columns.
Big or small, standing or lying, it is the same shape.

learn.hook: Seven pieces, one square, endless pictures! A tangram can become a cat, a boat or a rocket.
points: A tangram is a square puzzle cut into 7 pieces.
It has 5 triangles, 1 square and 1 slanting 4-sided piece called a parallelogram.
The triangles come in sizes: 2 big, 1 middle-sized and 2 small.
Two small triangles can be joined to make the square piece.
We put the pieces side by side, without overlapping, to make animals, people and things.

example.q: How many of the 7 tangram pieces are NOT triangles?
steps: They are the square and the parallelogram.

learn.reallife: Tangrams are a puzzle game from long ago. You can cut one from a square of paper and play with your friends.

games.title: Tangram facts
items: 5 are triangles, but there is also a square and a parallelogram.
Two small triangles can make a square.
Put their long sides together and you get a square.
It has 2 big triangles, 1 middle-sized one and 2 small ones.
The pieces lie flat side by side without covering each other.
Two small triangles can join to make a bigger triangle.
Join them along a short side and they make the middle-sized triangle.

items.text: The only piece with 4 equal sides is the ___.

quiz.q: How many pieces are there in a tangram?
quiz.explain: A tangram has 7 pieces: 5 triangles, 1 square and 1 parallelogram.
steps: A tangram has 5 triangles, 1 square and 1 parallelogram.

quiz.q: How many of the tangram pieces are triangles?
quiz.explain: 2 big + 1 middle + 2 small = 5 triangles.

quiz.q: Which shape can you make by joining the long sides of the 2 small tangram triangles?
quiz.explain: Two small triangles joined along their long sides make a square, the same size as the square piece.
steps: Join them along their long sides.
They make a square, the same size as the square piece.
quiz.mistake: Thinks joining triangles always makes a bigger triangle

quiz.q: Kabir makes a boat using 3 triangles and 1 square. How many corners do these pieces have altogether?
quiz.explain: 3 triangles have 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 corners. The square has 4. 9 + 4 = 13.

quiz.q: Which tangram piece is NOT a triangle and NOT a square?
quiz.explain: The parallelogram is the slanting 4-sided piece. It is not a triangle or a square.
steps: The parallelogram is the slanting 4-sided piece.
It is not a triangle and not a square.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that a tangram has a slanting piece

quiz.q: Aisha used all 7 pieces to make a cat. 5 of them were triangles. How many other pieces did she use?
quiz.explain: 7 pieces in all, 5 triangles. 7 − 5 = 2 other pieces: the square and the parallelogram.
quiz.mistake: Adds 7 and 5 instead of taking away

quiz.q: When we make a tangram picture, the pieces must ___.
quiz.explain: Tangram pieces lie flat, side by side, without covering one another.
steps: Tangram pieces lie flat, side by side.
They must not cover one another.
quiz.mistake: Thinks pieces can be stacked on top of each other

quiz.q: How many big triangles are there in a tangram?
quiz.explain: A tangram has 2 big triangles, 1 middle-sized triangle and 2 small triangles.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the number of big and small triangles

teach.ask: Gappu has 7 tangram pieces but doesn't know what they are. Tell him!
teach.praise: 5 triangles, a square and a parallelogram! I made a bird with them!
teach.nudge: Are all the pieces triangles? What other shapes are there?

revise.summary: A tangram is a square cut into 7 pieces: 5 triangles, 1 square and 1 parallelogram. We put them side by side to make pictures.
focus: Know the 7 tangram pieces.
Join pieces to make shapes.
Make pictures without overlapping.
remember: 2 small triangles make the square piece.
traps: Not all 7 pieces are triangles.
Pieces must not overlap.
Don't forget the slanting piece, the parallelogram.

learn.hook: The bangle stall has a huge heap. Guess first: 100? 200? 300?
points: First guess how many, then count to check your guess.
Count big heaps in groups of 10: 10, 20, 30 ... It is quicker and you do not lose track.
250 is 200 and 50 more. 280 is 200 and 80 more.
To find how many more make 300, count on from the number: 260 + 40 = 300.
To find which heap is more, compare the numbers: 270 is more than 250.

example.q: A stall has 260 balloons. How many more are needed to make 300?

learn.reallife: At a fair, ticket sellers count notes in bundles of 10 to be quick and correct.

quiz.q: A heap of bangles is counted in groups of 10. There are 24 groups. How many bangles?
quiz.explain: 24 groups of 10 = 240.

quiz.q: Raju guessed 200 marbles. He counted 230. How far off was he?
Which shows 250?
A stall has 275 kites. How many more to make 300?
Stall A has 268 toys. Stall B has 286. Which has more?
quiz.explain: Both have 2 hundreds. 8 tens is more than 6 tens, so 286 is more.

quiz.q: Why do we count a big heap in groups of 10?
options: It is quicker and easier to keep track
quiz.explain: Groups of 10 can be counted 10, 20, 30, so we do not lose count.
steps: Counting one by one in a big heap is slow, and we may lose count.
This is quicker and easier to keep track. The total does not change.
Answer: It is quicker and easier to keep track

quiz.q: Meena counted 20 groups of 10 and 7 more. How many?
A stall had 300 balloons. 40 flew away. How many are left?

teach.ask: Gappu sees a big pile of seeds at the mela. How can he count them without losing track?
teach.praise: Guess first, then count in tens: 10, 20, 30... Chirp!
teach.nudge: How can I group the seeds to count faster?

revise.summary: First guess how many, then count big heaps in groups of 10 to check. Count on to find how many more make 300.
focus: Estimate, then count in groups of 10.
Find how far off a guess was.
Find how many more make 300, or how many are left.
traps: Don't write the number of groups as the answer.
Don't write 20 tens and 7 as 2007. It is 207.
Groups of 10 do not change the total.

learn.hook: A cinema hall can have hundreds of seats! Let's learn to read and write such big numbers.
points: We can count in hundreds: 100, 200, 300 ... up to 900.
A 3-digit number has a hundreds digit, a tens digit and a ones digit.
We read 457 as 'four hundred fifty-seven'.
The smallest 3-digit number is 100 and the largest is 999.
After 999 comes 1000, our first 4-digit number.

example.q: Write 'six hundred eight' in numbers.
steps: No tens, so the tens digit is 0

learn.reallife: Bus numbers, house numbers and the price of a school bag often have 3 digits.

items.text: Eight hundred twenty in numbers is ___.

quiz.q: Count in hundreds: 200, 300, 400, ___
quiz.explain: Each step adds 1 hundred. 400 + 100 = 500.

quiz.q: Write 'five hundred thirty-six' in numbers.
quiz.explain: Five hundred is 500, thirty is 30 and six is 6. 500 + 30 + 6 = 536.
quiz.mistake: Writes 500 and then 36 next to it

quiz.q: Write 'seven hundred four' in numbers.
quiz.explain: 7 hundreds, no tens and 4 ones. The 0 holds the tens place: 704.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 0 in the tens place

quiz.q: What number comes just after 599?
quiz.explain: 1 more than 599 is 600. The 9 ones and 9 tens roll over into one more hundred.
steps: 599 + 1: the 9 ones and 9 tens roll over into one more hundred.
quiz.mistake: Writes 5 and then 100 next to it

quiz.q: Which is the largest 3-digit number?
quiz.explain: 999 has the biggest digit, 9, in every place. 1000 has 4 digits.
steps: The largest 3-digit number has 9 in every place.
1000 has 4 digits, so it is not a 3-digit number.

quiz.q: How do you read 860?
quiz.explain: 860 is 8 hundreds and 6 tens, so we say eight hundred sixty.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the 0 or reads the digits in the wrong places

quiz.q: A cinema has 300 seats downstairs and 200 seats upstairs. How many seats are there in all?
quiz.explain: 3 hundreds and 2 hundreds make 5 hundreds. 300 + 200 = 500.

quiz.q: Count back in hundreds: 900, 800, 700, ___
quiz.explain: Each step takes away 1 hundred. 700 − 100 = 600.

teach.ask: Gappu sees 'five hundred forty-two' on a bus. How should he write it in numbers?
teach.praise: 542! Five hundreds, four tens and two ones. I can read buses now!
teach.nudge: Which digit goes first, and what does 'forty' become?

revise.summary: We count in hundreds up to 900. A 3-digit number has hundreds, tens and ones digits. The smallest is 100 and the largest is 999.
focus: Count on and back in hundreds.
Read and write number names up to 999.
Find the number just after or before.
traps: Don't write 500 and 36 side by side as 50036.
Don't forget the 0 in the empty tens place.
1000 is not a 3-digit number.

learn.hook: 347 can be 300 + 47, or 340 + 7, or 3 hundreds 4 tens 7 ones. How many ways can you find?
points: Fill missing numbers on a path by finding the step: 312, 313, ___, 315.
Matchstick bundles show numbers: big bundles of 100, small bundles of 10, and loose sticks.
One number can be written in many number sentences: 365 = 300 + 65 = 360 + 5 = 300 + 60 + 5.
To write the number in a picture, count the hundreds, then tens, then ones.

example.q: A picture shows 3 big bundles, 2 small bundles and 6 loose sticks. What number is it?

learn.reallife: A cashier may count ₹347 as three ₹100 notes, four ₹10 notes and seven ₹1 coins.

quiz.q: Which number is missing? 356, 357, ___, 359
quiz.explain: Counting by 1: 357 + 1 = 358.

quiz.q: 3 bundles of 100, 0 bundles of 10 and 8 sticks show which number?
Which number sentence equals 365?
What is 200 + 150?
Which is NOT another way to write 284?
A picture shows 2 hundred-bundles, 13 ten-bundles and 0 loose sticks. What number?
quiz.mistake: Writes the counts side by side

quiz.q: Continue the path: 340, 350, 360, ___
quiz.explain: The path goes up by 10.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to write 246 in two different ways. Can you help him?
teach.nudge: Can I split 246 at the hundreds?

revise.summary: Numbers up to 400 can be shown with bundles of 100, 10 and loose sticks. One number can be written in many number sentences.
focus: Fill missing numbers on a path.
Read numbers from matchstick bundles.
Write a number in different ways.
traps: Don't leave out the zero.
Use place values, not just digits: 300 + 60 + 5, not 3 + 6 + 5.
Find the step of the path before filling it.

topics.title: Number slider and guess my number

learn.hook: Slide 1 more, 10 more, 20 less... Watch which digit changes!
points: Add or take away 1: only the ones digit changes (unless it crosses a ten). 245 + 1 = 246.
Add or take away 10: the tens digit changes. 245 + 10 = 255.
Adding 20 changes the tens digit by 2: 245 + 20 = 265.
In 'guess my number', use clues like 'more than' and 'less than' to narrow down the range.
Each good guess cuts the range: if it is between 200 and 300 and more than 250, try 275.

example.q: Start at 318. Add 2, then take away 10.

learn.reallife: Lift buttons and TV channel buttons go up and down by 1. Number sliders work the same way.

games.title: Which digit changes?
items: Adding 10 to 342 changes the tens digit.
Adding 1 to 342 changes the hundreds digit.

quiz.q: What is 237 + 10?
quiz.explain: Adding 10 makes the tens digit go up by 1.
steps: Adding 10 makes the tens digit go up by 1.

quiz.q: What is 452 − 2?
Which digit changes when you add 10 to 364?
quiz.explain: 364 + 10 = 374. Only the tens digit changed.

quiz.q: What is 196 + 20?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry into the hundreds

quiz.q: Guess my number: it is between 300 and 400. It is more than 350. It is less than 360. It ends in 5. What is it?
quiz.explain: Between 350 and 360, ending in 5: 355.

quiz.q: Guess my number: it is 10 less than 250. What is it?
Riya's guess is 200. Clue: 'More!' Her next guess is 300. Clue: 'Less!' What does she know?
quiz.explain: More than 200 and less than 300, so between them.
steps: Answer: The number is between 200 and 300

quiz.q: What is 300 − 1?
quiz.explain: One less than 300 is 299.

teach.ask: Gappu adds 10 to 426 and gets 427. What went wrong?
teach.praise: Adding 10 changes the tens, so 426 + 10 = 436! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Which digit should change when I add 10?

revise.summary: Adding or taking away 1 changes the ones digit. Adding or taking away 10 changes the tens digit. Clues like more than and less than help us guess a number.
focus: Add and take away 1, 2, 10 and 20.
Say which digit changes.
Use clues to narrow down a number.
traps: Don't forget to carry into the hundreds: 196 + 20 = 216.
Adding 10 does not change the ones digit.
Use every clue, not just the last one.

learn.hook: Pick any number, count the letters in its name, and keep going. You will always reach FOUR! Try it!
points: Magical count: write a number name, count its letters, and use that count as the next number.
Example: 23 → twenty-three (11 letters) → eleven (6) → six (3) → three (5) → five (4) → four (4).
FOUR has 4 letters, so the chain stops there.
The next hundred after a number is the first hundred bigger than it: after 347 comes 400.
We can show it on a number line or with bundles: 347 needs 3 more sticks to make 350, then 50 more to make 400. That is 53 in all.

example.q: Do the magical count for 7.

learn.reallife: Number-name games help you spell numbers correctly for cheques and forms.

quiz.q: How many letters are in 'fifteen'?
quiz.explain: F-I-F-T-E-E-N: 7 letters.

quiz.q: Magical count for 15: fifteen → 7 → ? What comes next?
quiz.explain: seven has 5 letters, so the next number is 5.
steps: fifteen has 7 letters, so the next number is 7.
quiz.mistake: Counts the letters of fifteen again

quiz.q: Where does every magical count end?
quiz.explain: four has exactly 4 letters, so the chain stops at 4.
steps: The chain keeps going: number → letters in its name.
So 4 gives 4 again. The chain stops at 4.

quiz.q: What is the next hundred after 438?
quiz.explain: 438 is between 400 and 500. The next hundred is 500.
steps: The next hundred is the first hundred bigger than 438.

quiz.q: How many more does 438 need to reach its next hundred?
Magical count for 40: forty → ?
quiz.explain: forty has 5 letters.
steps: Spell forty: f-o-r-t-y. There is no U.

quiz.q: What is the next hundred after 299?
Ravi has 3 bundles of 100 and 7 bundles of 10. How many more bundles of 10 make the next hundred?
quiz.explain: 370 + 30 = 400. That is 3 bundles of 10.

teach.ask: Gappu picked 99 for the magical count. What happens?
teach.praise: 99 → 10 → 3 → 5 → 4. Always four! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How many letters are in ninety-nine?

revise.summary: In a magical count, the next number is the number of letters in a number name. Every chain ends at 4. The next hundred is the first hundred bigger than a number.
focus: Do a magical count chain.
Find the next hundred.
Find how many more reach the next hundred.
remember: four has 4 letters, so the chain stops at 4.
traps: Forty has no U: f-o-r-t-y has 5 letters.
The next hundred is bigger, not the hundred before.
Count bundles, not sticks, when asked for bundles.

learn.hook: Where does 243 live on the number line? Between which neighbours?
points: To place 216 on a line, find 210 and 220, then go 6 steps past 210.
235 lies between 200 and 300. It is also between 200 and 250.
The distance to the next hundred: 387 → 390 is 3, 390 → 400 is 10. So 13.
Compare by jumping: 393 to 400 is a jump of 7, so 400 is 7 more than 393.

example.q: How far is 387 from 400?

learn.reallife: Milestones on highways are like a number line: you can see how far the next town is.

games.title: How far to the next hundred?

quiz.q: Between which two tens does 243 lie?
quiz.explain: 243 is 3 more than 240 and 7 less than 250.
steps: Find the tens on each side of 243.
243 is 3 more than 240 and 7 less than 250.
quiz.mistake: Picks the hundreds instead of the tens

quiz.q: 235 is between 200 and 300. Is it closer to 200 or to 250?
quiz.explain: 235 is 15 away from 250 but 35 away from 200.

quiz.q: How far is 387 from 400?
How much bigger is 400 than 393?
Which number is between 250 and 300?
quiz.explain: 257 is more than 250 and less than 300.
steps: We need a number more than 250 and less than 300.
216 and 235 are less than 250. 329 is more than 300.

quiz.q: On a line from 210 to 220, where is 216?
steps: So start at 210 and go 6 steps forward.

quiz.q: Which hundred is 329 closer to, 300 or 400?
quiz.explain: 329 is 29 away from 300 but 71 away from 400.

quiz.q: Jump from 365 by 5, then by 30. Where do you land?

teach.ask: Gappu is at 376 on a number line and wants to fly to 400. How far must he go?
teach.praise: 376 to 380 is 4, 380 to 400 is 20, so 24! Chirp!
teach.nudge: What is the next ten after 376?

revise.summary: To place a number on a line, find the tens on each side. Jump to the next ten, then to the hundred, to find how far apart numbers are.
focus: Find the tens or hundreds a number lies between.
Find the distance to the next hundred.
Place a number on a line.
traps: Don't look only at the hundreds.
Do both jumps, not just one.
Count from the right end of the line.

learn.hook: Farooq Chacha arranges barfis in neat rows. Counting is easy when the rows are equal!
points: Sweets in equal rows can be counted row by row: 5 rows of 10 is 50.
If a tray holds 100 and has 80, it needs 20 more to be full.
After filling, add to find the new total: 3 full trays of 100 and 1 tray of 60 is 360.
Numbers between 400 and 500 sit after 400 on the line: 450 is halfway, 480 is near 500.

example.q: A tray holds 100 laddoos in 10 rows of 10. It has 7 full rows. How many more to fill it?

learn.reallife: Sweet shops arrange sweets in rows on trays so that they can count stock quickly.

quiz.q: A tray has 8 rows of 10 jalebis. How many jalebis?
quiz.explain: 8 rows of 10 = 80.

quiz.q: A tray holds 100 barfis. It has 64. How many more fill it?
Farooq Chacha has 4 full trays of 100 and fills another tray with 25. How many sweets in all?
Which number is halfway between 400 and 500?
quiz.explain: 450 is 50 more than 400 and 50 less than 500.

quiz.q: Is 480 closer to 400 or 500?
quiz.explain: 480 is 20 away from 500 and 80 away from 400.
steps: 20 is less than 80, so 480 is closer to 500.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the hundreds digit

quiz.q: A tray has 3 rows of 10 and 4 more. How many sweets?
A tray had 90 sweets. 10 more were added. Now 2 full trays of 100 and this tray. Total?
Which number lies between 430 and 440?
quiz.explain: 436 is more than 430 and less than 440.
steps: We need a number more than 430 and less than 440.
403 and 426 are less than 430. 446 is more than 440.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number with the right digits in the wrong places

teach.ask: Gappu has a tray of 100 places and 72 seeds in it. How many more fill the tray?
teach.praise: 72 to 80 is 8, 80 to 100 is 20, so 28! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How far is 72 from the next ten?

revise.summary: Sweets in equal rows are counted row by row. A tray of 100 that has some needs the rest to be full.
focus: Count rows of 10.
Find how many more fill a tray of 100.
Place numbers between 400 and 500 on a line.
traps: Don't add rows and 10. 8 rows of 10 is 80, not 18.
Don't pick 440 for halfway.
Don't swap tens and ones.

learn.hook: In this building, the house numbers follow a secret pattern. Can you crack it?
points: In our building, each row (floor) has 10 houses. House numbers go up by 1 to the right.
Going up one floor adds 10. Going down one floor takes away 10.
So moving left or right changes the ones digit, and moving up or down changes the tens digit.
To find a house, look at its tens to find the floor row and its ones to find the column.
'Who am I?' riddles use clues about digits and places.

example.q: The ground row has 301 to 310. House 324 is how many floors up, and in which column?
steps: 324 is the 4th house in that row

learn.reallife: Hotel rooms are often numbered so the first digits tell the floor and the last digits tell the room.

quiz.q: In the building, floors go up by 10. What house is directly above 342?
quiz.explain: Up one floor adds 10: 342 + 10 = 352.

quiz.q: Which house is to the right of 358?
quiz.explain: Right adds 1: 358 + 1 = 359.

quiz.q: Moving down one floor from 375 gives which house?
quiz.explain: Down takes away 10.
steps: Going down one floor takes away 10.

quiz.q: When you move left or right in this building, which digit changes?
quiz.explain: Left and right are steps of 1.
steps: Left and right are steps of 1.
Adding or taking away 1 changes the ones digit.

quiz.explain: 336 is between 331 and 340.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the ones digit

quiz.q: Who am I? I am 2 floors above 314.
steps: Each floor up adds 10. 2 floors up adds 20.

quiz.q: Who am I? My hundreds digit is 3, my tens digit is 1 more than 3, my ones digit is 0.
quiz.explain: Tens = 4. Number = 340.
quiz.mistake: Puts the digits in the wrong places

quiz.q: House numbers in a column: 305, 315, 325, ___. What comes next?
quiz.explain: Going up a column adds 10.

teach.ask: Gappu lives in house 347. His friend lives one floor up, one house to the right. Which house is that?
teach.nudge: What changes when I go up one floor?

revise.summary: In the building, moving right adds 1 and moving up a floor adds 10. Left or right changes the ones digit; up or down changes the tens digit.
focus: Find the house above, below, left or right.
Find the row a house is in.
Solve 'Who am I?' digit riddles.
remember: Ground row 301-310. 324 is 2 floors up, column 4.
traps: Don't add 1 when going up a floor. Add 10.
Don't mix up rows and columns.
Put each digit in the right place.

learn.hook: 275 laddoos to pack. Big boxes hold 100, small boxes hold 10. How many of each?
points: Pack the biggest boxes first: 275 = 2 boxes of 100, 7 boxes of 10 and 5 loose.
10 tens make 1 hundred. If we open a box of 100, we get 10 boxes of 10.
So 2 hundreds = 20 tens, and 3 hundreds 4 tens = 34 tens.
Numbers from 200 to 300 that have a 5: 205, 215, ... and all of 250 to 259. There are 19.
Show and tell: one child asks 'How many tens in 340?' and the next answers and asks a new question.

example.q: Pack 342 sweets. How many boxes of 100, boxes of 10 and loose sweets?

learn.reallife: Bakeries pack biscuits in packets of 10 and cartons of 100 so they can count stock quickly.

quiz.q: How many boxes of 100 are needed to pack 438 sweets (with tens and loose)?
How many tens are there in 1 hundred?
quiz.explain: 10 tens make 1 hundred.

quiz.q: Open 3 boxes of 100. How many boxes of 10 do you get?
quiz.explain: Each hundred gives 10 tens: 10 + 10 + 10 = 30.
steps: Each box of 100 opens into 10 boxes of 10.

quiz.q: How many tens are there in 250 altogether?
quiz.explain: 200 = 20 tens and 50 = 5 tens. 20 + 5 = 25 tens.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the tens digit

quiz.q: Which number between 200 and 300 does NOT have a 5?
quiz.explain: 267 has digits 2, 6 and 7. No 5.
steps: Look at every digit for a 5.
256 has 5 in tens. 295 has 5 in ones. 215 has 5 in ones.
quiz.mistake: Misses the 5 in the tens place

quiz.q: How many numbers from 250 to 259 are there?
quiz.explain: 250, 251, ..., 259: that is 10 numbers.

quiz.q: How many numbers between 200 and 300 contain the digit 5?
Show and tell: 'I have 5 boxes of 100, 0 boxes of 10 and 6 loose.' What is the number?

teach.ask: Gappu opened a box of 100 seeds. He found smaller packets of 10 inside. How many packets?
teach.praise: 10 packets of 10 make 100! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How many tens make one hundred?

revise.summary: Pack the biggest boxes first: 275 = 2 boxes of 100, 7 boxes of 10 and 5 loose. 10 tens make 1 hundred.
focus: Split a number into hundreds, tens and ones.
Find how many tens are in a number.
Find numbers with a given digit.
traps: Don't count tens when asked for hundreds.
Don't forget 250 when counting 250 to 259.
Don't leave out the zero: 506, not 56.

learn.hook: Every digit lives in its own house: Hundreds House, Tens House or Ones House!
points: In 358, the 3 is in the hundreds place, the 5 is in the tens place and the 8 is in the ones place.
358 = 300 + 50 + 8. This is called the expanded form.
The same digit has a different value in a different place. In 535, the first 5 is worth 500 and the last 5 is worth 5.
Zero keeps a place empty: 405 has 0 tens.

example.q: Write 642 in expanded form.

learn.reallife: ₹100 notes, ₹10 notes and ₹1 coins work just like hundreds, tens and ones.

quiz.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in 739?
quiz.explain: 7 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 7 hundreds = 700.
steps: The 7 is in the hundreds place.
quiz.mistake: Gives the digit instead of its value

quiz.q: Which is the expanded form of 481?
quiz.explain: 4 hundreds, 8 tens and 1 one: 400 + 80 + 1.
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits without their place values

quiz.q: 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 9 ones make which number?
quiz.explain: 400 + 0 + 9 = 409. The 0 keeps the tens place.
quiz.mistake: Leaves out the 0 in the tens place

quiz.q: Harpreet has three ₹100 notes, two ₹10 notes and six ₹1 coins. How much money does she have?
quiz.mistake: Counts the notes and coins instead of their values

quiz.q: In 555, what is the value of the 5 in the tens place?
quiz.explain: A 5 in the tens place means 5 tens = 50.
steps: The 5 in the tens place means 5 tens.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every 5 in 555 has the same value

quiz.q: How many hundreds are there in 800?
quiz.explain: 800 = 8 hundreds.

quiz.q: Which number has 6 in the ones place?
quiz.explain: The ones place is the last digit. Only 406 ends in 6.
steps: The ones place is the last digit.
quiz.mistake: Looks for 6 in any place, not just the ones place

quiz.q: What number is 600 + 5 + 30?
quiz.explain: 600 is 6 hundreds, 30 is 3 tens and 5 is 5 ones. Put them in their places: 635.
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits in the order they are given, not by place

teach.ask: Gappu thinks both 5s in 535 are worth the same. Is he right? Explain to him.
teach.praise: One 5 is 500 and the other is just 5! The place decides the value!
teach.nudge: Where is each 5 sitting? Does that change what it is worth?

revise.summary: In a 3-digit number, each digit has a place: hundreds, tens or ones. The value of a digit depends on its place. 358 = 300 + 50 + 8.
focus: Find the value of a digit.
Write numbers in expanded form.
Use 0 to keep an empty place.
remember: In 535, the first 5 is 500 and the last 5 is 5.
traps: Don't give the digit when asked its value.
The same digit in different places has different values.
Don't leave out the 0 in the tens place.

learn.hook: Two trains, 845 and 854 passengers. Which one is more crowded? Let's find out!
points: To compare, look at the hundreds first: 512 > 498 because 5 hundreds is more than 4 hundreds.
If the hundreds are the same, compare the tens. If the tens are also the same, compare the ones.
> means 'greater than' and < means 'less than'. The open side faces the bigger number.
100 more than 345 is 445. 10 less than 345 is 335.

example.q: Arrange 607, 670 and 760 from smallest to biggest.
steps: 607 and 670 both have 6 hundreds. Tens: 0 and 7.

learn.reallife: Comparing prices helps you pick the cheaper cycle, and comparing scores tells you which team won.

games.title: Bigger or smaller?
items: Both have 6 hundreds. 3 tens is more than 0 tens, so 630 > 603.
The hundreds digit goes up by 1: 245 + 100 = 345.
Both have 9 hundreds. 0 tens is less than 9 tens, so 909 < 990.
Same digits in the same places make equal numbers.

quiz.q: Which is greater: 512 or 498?
quiz.explain: Compare hundreds first. 5 hundreds is more than 4 hundreds, so 512 is greater.
steps: 5 hundreds is more, so 512 is greater.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the 9s in 498 and thinks it is bigger

quiz.q: Which sign makes this true? 630 ___ 603
quiz.explain: Same hundreds. 3 tens is more than 0 tens, so 630 > 603.
steps: 3 tens is more, so 630 is greater.

quiz.q: What is 100 more than 456?
quiz.explain: 100 more adds 1 to the hundreds digit: 456 + 100 = 556.
steps: 100 more adds 1 to the hundreds digit.

quiz.q: What is 10 less than 382?
quiz.explain: 10 less takes 1 away from the tens digit: 382 − 10 = 372.
steps: 10 less takes 1 from the tens digit.

quiz.q: Which is the smallest: 415, 451, 514 or 541?
quiz.explain: 415 and 451 have the fewest hundreds (4). Between them, 1 ten is less than 5 tens, so 415 is smallest.
steps: Compare 415 and 451 by tens: 1 ten < 5 tens.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the last digit

quiz.q: The Delhi train has 845 passengers and the Mumbai train has 854. Which train has more passengers?
quiz.explain: Both have 8 hundreds. 5 tens is more than 4 tens, so 854 is more.

quiz.q: Which list goes from smallest to biggest?
quiz.explain: 230 has 2 hundreds, so it is smallest. 302 has 0 tens and 320 has 2 tens, so 302 comes before 320.
quiz.mistake: Thinks numbers with the same digits are all equal

quiz.q: Using the digits 4, 7 and 2 once each, what is the biggest number you can make?
quiz.explain: Put the biggest digit in the hundreds place, the next in tens, the smallest in ones: 742.
quiz.mistake: Puts the biggest digit in the ones place

teach.ask: Gappu thinks 609 is bigger than 690 because 9 is a big digit. Help him compare!
teach.praise: Same hundreds, so I check the tens! 690 is bigger. Thank you!
teach.nudge: Which place should I look at after the hundreds?

revise.summary: To compare 3-digit numbers, look at the hundreds first, then tens, then ones. The open side of > or < faces the bigger number.
focus: Compare and order 3-digit numbers.
Use > and < correctly.
Find 100 more, 100 less, 10 more and 10 less.
traps: Don't compare the ones digit first.
Don't mix up > and <.
Numbers with the same digits are not equal.

learn.hook: To compare 452 and 458, do you need to look at the hundreds? No! Find the place that decides.
points: To compare, look from the left. The first place where the digits differ decides.
452 and 458: hundreds same, tens same, ones differ. The ones place decides.
317 and 371: hundreds same, tens differ. The tens place decides.
With digits 1, 2 and 3 (no repeating), we can make 6 numbers: 123, 132, 213, 231, 312, 321.
If digits can repeat, we can make more numbers, like 111, 112 and 333.

example.q: Make all 3-digit numbers with 4, 5 and 6, using each digit once.

learn.reallife: Bus numbers, house numbers and locker codes are made by arranging digits.

quiz.q: Comparing 645 and 649, which place decides?
quiz.explain: Hundreds same, tens same, ones 5 and 9 differ.
steps: Ones: 5 and 9 differ. The ones place decides.

quiz.q: Comparing 382 and 328, which place decides?
quiz.explain: Hundreds both 3. Tens 8 and 2 differ.

quiz.q: Comparing 719 and 791, which is bigger?
quiz.explain: Tens decide: 9 tens is more than 1 ten.

quiz.q: How many 3-digit numbers can be made with 2, 5 and 8, using each once?
Using 3, 0 and 6 once each, which order does NOT give a 3-digit number?
quiz.explain: Starting with 0 gives 036, which is just 36, a 2-digit number.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a leading zero is fine

quiz.q: Using 4 and 7, with repeats allowed, how many 2-digit numbers can you make?
steps: Repeats allowed. Tens digit: 4 or 7. Ones digit: 4 or 7.

quiz.q: Using 1, 5 and 9 once each, what is the smallest number?
quiz.explain: Smallest digit first: 1, then 5, then 9.
steps: For the smallest number, put the smallest digit first.

quiz.q: Using digits 3 and 8 with repeats, which is the biggest 3-digit number?
quiz.explain: Repeats allowed, so use 8 in every place.
steps: For the biggest number, use the biggest digit, 8, in every place.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to compare 527 and 572. Does he need to check the hundreds or the tens?
teach.praise: Hundreds are the same, the tens decide: 572 is bigger! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Which place is the first one that is different?

revise.summary: To compare, look from the left: the first place where digits differ decides. We can make many numbers from a few digits.
focus: Say which place decides a comparison.
Make all numbers from given digits.
Find the smallest or biggest number from digits.
remember: With repeats, we can make more, like 111 and 333.
traps: Don't always look at the hundreds.
A number starting with 0 is not a 3-digit number.
Don't forget the repeated ones when repeats are allowed.

learn.hook: Each rakhi needs 3 beads and 1 thread. How many beads for 10 rakhis?
points: Count things in a picture by making groups: 3 groups of 4 diyas is 12.
If 1 rakhi needs 3 beads, 5 rakhis need 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 15 beads. That is 5 × 3.
10 rakhis need 10 × 3 = 30 beads.
If we have only 12 beads and each rakhi needs 3, we can make 4 rakhis, because 4 × 3 = 12.
Draw your own equal groups, then write the multiplication: 4 plates of 2 sweets is 4 × 2 = 8.

example.q: Each rakhi needs 2 flowers. Seema has 14 flowers. How many rakhis can she make?

learn.reallife: Before a festival, families work out how many diyas, rakhis or sweets they need for everyone.

quiz.q: 1 rakhi needs 4 beads. How many beads for 5 rakhis?
steps: 1 rakhi needs 4 beads. There are 5 rakhis.

quiz.q: 1 rakhi needs 3 beads. How many beads for 10 rakhis?
Each rakhi needs 2 flowers. Amit has 10 flowers. How many rakhis can he make?
quiz.explain: 5 × 2 = 10, so 5 rakhis.

quiz.q: Each rakhi needs 5 sequins. Rani has 22 sequins. How many FULL rakhis can she make?
quiz.explain: 4 × 5 = 20 and 5 × 5 = 25 is too many. So 4 rakhis, with 2 sequins left.

quiz.q: A picture has 3 rows of 4 diyas. How many diyas?
steps: 3 rows with 4 diyas in each row.

quiz.q: Which drawing shows 4 × 3?
options: 4 laddoos and 3 plates in one heap
quiz.explain: 4 × 3 means 4 groups of 3.
steps: 4 plates with 3 laddoos each is 4 groups of 3.

quiz.q: Each rakhi needs 1 thread and 2 beads. For 6 rakhis, how many beads?
quiz.explain: 6 × 2 = 12 beads.
steps: Each rakhi needs 2 beads. There are 6 rakhis.

quiz.q: Kavita has 15 beads and makes rakhis with 3 beads each. How many rakhis?
quiz.explain: 3 × 5 = 15, so 5 rakhis.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to make 5 nests. Each nest needs 4 twigs. How can he find how many twigs he needs?
teach.praise: 5 groups of 4 is 20 twigs! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How many twigs go in each nest, and how many nests?

revise.summary: When each rakhi needs the same number of beads, we multiply to find how many beads in all. We can also find how many rakhis can be made from a number of beads.
focus: Count things in equal groups.
Find how many beads many rakhis need.
Find how many rakhis some beads can make.
traps: Don't add the two numbers. Multiply.
4 × 3 is not 4 + 3.
Count only what is asked, like beads and not threads.

learn.hook: Riya has 3 brothers, and each one gets 2 sweets on Raksha Bandhan. How many sweets does she need?
points: Equal groups have the same number of things in each group.
We can find the total by adding the same number again and again: 3 groups of 2 is 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.
Adding equal groups like this is called multiplication.
We write 3 groups of 2 as 3 × 2 = 6. We say 'three times two is six'.
If the groups are not the same size, they are not equal groups.

example.q: Meena makes 4 rakhis. Each rakhi has 5 beads. How many beads does she use?

learn.reallife: Sweets in a box, eggs in a tray and chairs in rows are all arranged in equal groups.

quiz.q: Riya has 3 brothers. She gives each brother 2 laddoos. How many laddoos does she give?
quiz.explain: 3 groups of 2: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6. That is 3 × 2 = 6.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 2 instead of making 3 groups of 2

quiz.q: Which means the same as 4 + 4 + 4?
quiz.explain: There are 3 fours added together. That is 3 groups of 4, or 3 × 4.
quiz.mistake: Uses the number being added for both parts of the multiplication

quiz.q: There are 5 plates with 3 puris on each plate. How many puris are there?
There are 2 boxes with 10 rakhis in each box. How many rakhis in all?
Which of these shows EQUAL groups?
quiz.explain: Equal groups have the same number in each group. Only 4, 4 and 4 are all the same.
steps: Equal groups have the same number in each group.
4, 3, 5 and 6, 4 and 1, 2, 3 are not the same.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any set of bags makes equal groups

quiz.q: Arjun says 4 × 2 means 4 groups of 2. What is 4 × 2?
Aisha's thali has 3 rows of sweets with 6 sweets in each row. Which addition shows the total?
quiz.explain: There are 3 rows, and each row has 6. So we add 6 three times: 6 + 6 + 6.
steps: 3 rows, with 6 sweets in each row.
quiz.mistake: Adds the number of rows instead of the number in each row

quiz.q: Kabir buys 5 rakhis for ₹10 each. How much does he pay?

teach.ask: Gappu sees 4 nests with 3 eggs in each. He wants to know how many eggs there are without counting one by one. How?
teach.praise: 4 groups of 3 is 12! Multiplying is so quick!
teach.nudge: Does every nest have the same number? What can I do with that?

revise.summary: Equal groups have the same number in each group. Adding equal groups again and again is multiplication: 3 groups of 2 is 3 × 2 = 6.
focus: Spot equal groups.
Write repeated addition as multiplication.
Find totals of equal groups.
traps: Don't add 3 and 2 when there are 3 groups of 2.
Groups of different sizes are not equal groups.
Add the number in each row, not the number of rows.

learn.hook: 18 laddoos and 9 friends. Will everyone get the same? Let us share fairly!
points: 3 plates with 3 laddoos each is 3 × 3 = 9 laddoos.
Sharing equally: 18 laddoos among 9 friends gives 2 each, because 9 × 2 = 18.
Draw plates and put one sweet on each plate in turn until all are used: 20 kaju katlis on 5 plates gives 4 each.
Grouping: 12 wheels make 6 cycles, because each cycle needs 2 wheels. 12 ÷ 2 = 6.
Check if there is enough: 5 friends, 2 sweets each, need 10. With 8 sweets, 2 more are needed.

example.q: 20 kaju katlis are shared on 5 plates. How many on each plate?

learn.reallife: At a Raksha Bandhan lunch, sweets are shared so every brother and sister gets the same.

quiz.q: 18 laddoos are shared equally among 9 friends. How many does each get?
quiz.explain: 9 × 2 = 18, so each gets 2.

quiz.q: 20 kaju katlis are put equally on 5 plates. How many on each?
How many cycles can be made from 12 wheels?
quiz.explain: Each cycle needs 2 wheels. 12 ÷ 2 = 6.

quiz.q: How many cycles can be made from 10 wheels?
3 plates have 3 laddoos each. Which shows this?
quiz.explain: 3 groups of 3 is 3 × 3 = 9.
steps: 3 plates with 3 laddoos each = 3 groups of 3.

quiz.q: 6 friends each want 3 jalebis. Mummy has 15. How many more does she need?
quiz.explain: 6 × 3 = 18 needed. 18 − 15 = 3 more.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number needed, not the extra

quiz.q: 24 rasgullas are shared among 6 children. How many each?
Mira has 14 barfis for 7 friends. Does each get 2?
quiz.explain: 7 × 2 = 14, so all 14 are shared with none left.
steps: All 14 are shared and none are left.

teach.ask: Gappu has 12 berries for 4 friends. How should he share them fairly?
teach.praise: Give one to each, again and again. Everyone gets 3! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How do I make sure everyone gets the same?

revise.summary: Sharing equally means each one gets the same. We share by putting one on each plate in turn, or by thinking of a multiplication fact.
focus: Share things equally.
Make groups of a size, like 2 wheels per cycle.
Check if there is enough for everyone.
traps: Don't add or take away when sharing.
Use the multiplication fact to check: 5 × 4 = 20.
When asked how many more, give the extra needed.

learn.hook: Diwali diyas in neat rows look beautiful, and they also help you multiply!
points: An array puts things in rows. 3 rows of 4 is 3 × 4 = 12.
Turn the array around: 4 rows of 3 is also 12. So 3 × 4 = 4 × 3.
× 2 is the same as doubling: 2 × 7 = 14.
× 10 puts a 0 at the end: 6 × 10 = 60.
Learn the tables of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 by skip counting.

example.q: Diwali diyas are placed in 4 rows with 6 diyas in each row. How many diyas?

learn.reallife: Seats in a bus, squares on a chocolate bar and windows on a building are all arrays.

quiz.q: There are 3 rows of chairs with 5 chairs in each row. How many chairs?
What is 4 × 3?
quiz.explain: 4 groups of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12.

quiz.q: Which is the same as 2 × 6?
quiz.explain: Turning an array around does not change the total. 2 × 6 = 6 × 2 = 12.
steps: Turning an array around does not change the total.
2 + 6 = 8, so it is not the same.
quiz.mistake: Thinks changing the order changes the answer

quiz.q: What is 7 × 10?
quiz.explain: 7 tens make 70. Multiplying by 10 puts a 0 at the end.
quiz.mistake: Adds 7 and 10, or puts two zeros

quiz.q: Arjun has 5 packets with 4 pencils in each. How many pencils does he have?
What is double 9?
quiz.explain: Double means 2 times. 9 + 9 = 18.

quiz.q: A rangoli has 4 rows of dots with 4 dots in each row. How many dots are there?
Meena knows that 3 × 5 = 15. What is 3 × 6?
quiz.explain: 3 × 6 is 3 groups of 6. That is 1 more in each of the 3 groups than 3 × 5, so add 3: 15 + 3 = 18.
steps: Each of the 3 groups gets 1 more: add 3
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of adding 1 to each of the 3 groups

teach.ask: Gappu arranged his seeds in 2 rows of 5. His friend says 5 rows of 2 is the same amount. Who is right?
teach.praise: 2 × 5 and 5 × 2 are both 10! Turning the rows around keeps the total the same.
teach.nudge: How many seeds are there each way? Is the total the same?

revise.summary: An array puts things in rows. 3 rows of 4 is 3 × 4 = 12, and turning it gives 4 × 3 = 12 too.
focus: Find totals from arrays.
Know that order does not change the product.
Use doubles and × 10.
traps: Changing the order does not change the answer.
Double 9 is 18, not 99.

learn.hook: A frog that jumps 2 steps each time lands on 2, 4, 6, 8... That's skip counting!
points: Skip counting means jumping by the same number each time.
By 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20 ... These numbers end in 5 or 0.
By 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40 ... These numbers end in 0.
Skip counting is a quick way to count equal groups.

example.q: Count the fingers on 6 hands by skip counting.
steps: Each hand has 5 fingers, so count by 5s.

learn.reallife: Counting pairs of shoes by 2s or ₹10 notes by 10s is skip counting.

quiz.q: Skip count by 2s: 12, 14, 16, ___
quiz.explain: Each jump adds 2. 16 + 2 = 18.
steps: Skip count by 2s: each jump adds 2.

quiz.q: Skip count by 5s: 25, 30, 35, ___
quiz.explain: Each jump adds 5. 35 + 5 = 40.
steps: Skip count by 5s: each jump adds 5.

quiz.q: Which number is missing? 4, 8, ___, 16, 20
quiz.explain: The numbers go up by 4 each time. 8 + 4 = 12, and 12 + 4 = 16.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the pattern goes up by 2

quiz.q: How many wheels do 7 bicycles have? Count by 2s.
quiz.explain: Each bicycle has 2 wheels. 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14.
Each jump adds 10. 50 + 10 = 60.

quiz.q: Which of these numbers will you say when counting by 5s from 5?
quiz.explain: Counting by 5s gives numbers ending in 5 or 0. Only 35 ends in 5 or 0.
steps: Counting by 5s gives numbers that end in 5 or 0.
23, 42 and 51 do not end in 5 or 0.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice that 5s end in 5 or 0

quiz.q: Joseph counts by 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12. What comes next?
quiz.explain: Each jump adds 3. 12 + 3 = 15.

quiz.q: Harpreet has 4 packets of rakhis with 5 rakhis in each. Count by 5s. How many rakhis?
quiz.explain: 5, 10, 15, 20. Four jumps of 5 make 20.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to count 30 grains quickly. He has heard of skip counting. What is it?
teach.praise: Hop, hop, hop by the same number! Counting is faster now!
teach.nudge: Do I jump by a different number each time, or the same number?

revise.summary: Skip counting means jumping by the same number each time. It is a quick way to count equal groups.
focus: Skip count by 2s, 3s, 4s, 5s and 10s.
Find missing numbers in a skip count.
Know which numbers come in the 5s and 10s.
traps: Don't add 1 instead of the jump size.
Find the jump size first: 4, 8, 12 goes up by 4.
Don't count one jump too many.

learn.hook: A frog jumps 3 steps each time: 3, 6, 9, 12... That is the table of 3!
points: Skip counting by 3 on a number line: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30.
Each landing point gives a table fact: the 4th jump of 6 lands on 24, so 4 × 6 = 24.
To find the jump size, look at the gap between landings: 8, 16, 24 has jumps of 8.

example.q: A pattern goes 6, 12, 18, 24. What is the jump size, and what comes next?

learn.reallife: Egg trays of 6 and chocolate bars of 8 squares make the tables of 6 and 8 handy.

quiz.q: Skip count by 4: 4, 8, 12, ___
steps: Skip count by 4: each jump adds 4.

quiz.q: A frog jumps by 3 from 0. Where is it after 6 jumps?
quiz.explain: 6 jumps of 3 = 6 × 3 = 18.

quiz.q: What is 7 × 6?
What is 5 × 8?
A pattern: 8, 16, 24, 32. What is the jump size?
quiz.explain: Each number is 8 more than the one before.

quiz.q: Which number is in the table of 3?
steps: 21 is in the list. 20, 22 and 25 are not.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number from the 5 table

quiz.q: Which number is in both the 4 table and the 6 table?
quiz.mistake: Picks a number in one table only

quiz.q: Jumps land on 6, 12, 18, ___, 30. What is missing?

teach.ask: Gappu jumps 4 steps at a time from 0. Where will he be after 5 jumps, and what table fact is that?
teach.nudge: What numbers do I land on?

revise.summary: Skip counting by 3, 4, 6 and 8 on a number line gives their tables. Each landing point is a table fact.
focus: Say the tables of 3, 4, 6 and 8.
Find where a frog lands after some jumps.
Find the jump size from a pattern.
traps: Don't stop one jump early.
Don't add the numbers: 5 × 8 is 40, not 13.
Jump size is the gap, not the first number doubled.

learn.hook: A flower is at 24. Which equal jump gets you there in the fewest hops?
points: To reach 24 from 0 with equal jumps, you can jump by 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 or 12.
Bigger jumps need fewer hops: jumps of 8 reach 24 in 3 hops, jumps of 2 take 12 hops.
Some numbers, like 7, 11 and 13, are not in the table of 2, 3, 4 or any jump size bigger than 1 (except one giant jump of the whole number). To reach them with many equal jumps, only jumps of 1 work.
Stick-crossing: lay 3 sticks one way and 4 sticks across them. Count the crossing points: 12. So 3 × 4 = 12.
Stick crossings can help write tables of 5 to 10.

example.q: Which jump reaches 20 in the fewest hops: 2, 4 or 5?

learn.reallife: Sticks and lines crossing is an old Indian-style way of multiplying without a table chart.

games.title: Reach with equal jumps of 2 or 3?

quiz.q: A flower is at 24. Which jump size reaches it in the FEWEST hops?
quiz.explain: 24 ÷ 8 = 3 hops. The others need more hops.

quiz.q: How many hops of 6 reach 24?
Which number can you NOT reach from 0 with equal jumps of 2, 3, 4 or 5?
quiz.explain: 7 is not in the tables of 2, 3, 4 or 5. Only jumps of 1 (or one jump of 7) reach it.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every number can be reached

quiz.q: Which number can be reached only by jumps of 1 (if you must take more than one jump)?
quiz.explain: 13 is not in the table of any number from 2 to 12.
quiz.mistake: Picks an odd number that is in the 3 or 5 table

quiz.q: 3 sticks are laid one way and 4 sticks across them. How many crossing points?
quiz.explain: Each of the 3 sticks crosses all 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
steps: Each of the 3 sticks crosses all 4 sticks.

quiz.q: Stick-crossing for 6 × 7: 6 sticks one way and 7 across. How many crossings?
Ravi reaches 30 with jumps of 5. Asha reaches 30 with jumps of 10. Who takes fewer hops?
quiz.explain: Asha needs 3 hops. Ravi needs 6.
quiz.mistake: Thinks small jumps mean fewer hops

quiz.q: How many crossings for 9 × 5 sticks?

teach.ask: Gappu wants to reach a berry at 18 in the fewest equal hops. He can hop by 2, 3, 6 or 9. Which hop size should he choose?
teach.praise: Hops of 9! Just 2 hops: 9, 18! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Which jump sizes reach exactly 18?

revise.summary: To reach a number with equal jumps, the jump size must fit exactly. Bigger jumps need fewer hops. Stick crossings show multiplication facts.
focus: Find which jumps reach a number exactly.
Find how many hops it takes.
Use stick crossings for times tables.
remember: 24 can be reached by jumps of 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 or 12.
Jumps of 8 reach 24 in 3 hops. Jumps of 2 take 12 hops.
traps: Small jumps do not mean fewer hops.
Not every number can be reached by every jump.
Don't add the sticks. Count the crossings.

learn.hook: Without multiplying, can you tell the last digit of 7 × 5? Here is a secret!
points: In the 5 table, an even number times 5 ends in 0: 4 × 5 = 20.
An odd number times 5 ends in 5: 7 × 5 = 35.
Add the 2 table and the 3 table: 2 + 3 = 5, 4 + 6 = 10, 6 + 9 = 15. You get the 5 table!
Other pairs work too: the 2 table + the 4 table gives the 6 table; the 3 table + the 5 table gives the 8 table.

example.q: Does 8 × 5 end in 0 or 5?

learn.reallife: Counting ₹5 coins: an even number of them always makes a round ₹10, ₹20, ₹30...

quiz.q: What is the last digit of 9 × 5?
quiz.explain: 9 is odd, so 9 × 5 ends in 5. It is 45.

quiz.q: What is the last digit of 6 × 5?
quiz.explain: 6 is even, so it ends in 0. 6 × 5 = 30.

quiz.q: Which product ends in 5?
steps: Odd × 5 ends in 5. Even × 5 ends in 0.

quiz.q: Adding the 2 table and the 3 table gives which table?
quiz.explain: 2 + 3 = 5, so we get the 5 table.
steps: Add the 2 table and the 3 table: 2 + 3 = 5, 4 + 6 = 10, 6 + 9 = 15.

quiz.q: The 2 table + the 4 table gives which table?
steps: Add the 2 table and the 4 table: 2 + 4 = 6, 4 + 8 = 12.

quiz.q: Without working out, does 15 × 5 end in 0 or 5?
quiz.explain: 15 is odd, so the answer ends in 5. (It is 75.)

teach.ask: Gappu thinks 3 × 5 ends in 0. Can you explain the pattern to him?
teach.praise: Odd times 5 ends in 5, even times 5 ends in 0! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Is 3 odd or even?

revise.summary: In the 5 table, even × 5 ends in 0 and odd × 5 ends in 5. Adding two tables gives another table: 2 table + 3 table = 5 table.
focus: Tell if a 5-table answer ends in 0 or 5.
Add two tables to get a new table.
Use the pattern to check answers.
remember: 2 table + 4 table = 6 table. 3 table + 5 table = 8 table.
traps: Not every 5-table answer ends in 0.
Add the tables, don't multiply them: 2 + 3 = 5, not 6.
In 15 × 5, look at whether 15 is odd, not at its 5.

learn.hook: Save ₹5 every day. How many days to save ₹40 for a kite?
points: Sharing equally: 30 pencils among 6 children gives 5 each.
Equal jumps: a frog jumps 4 each time. 7 jumps take it to 28.
Saving: ₹5 a day for 8 days is ₹40. To save ₹40 at ₹5 a day, we need 8 days.
Some problems have two steps: 5 packets of 6 sweets is 30; give away 12; 18 are left.
Make your own problem: for 4 × 9 say 'There are 4 bags of 9 mangoes. How many mangoes?'

example.q: Rohan has 4 boxes of 6 crayons. He gives 10 to his sister. How many are left?

learn.reallife: Saving a fixed amount every day in a gullak (piggy bank) is how many children save for gifts.

games.title: Which problem fits?
pairs: 45 rupees, 5 rupees a day: how many days?

quiz.q: Asha saves ₹5 every day. How much does she save in 7 days?
Ravi wants ₹60 and saves ₹10 a day. How many days?
32 kites are shared equally among 8 children. How many each?
A frog makes equal jumps of 5 and lands on 45. How many jumps?
Mummy bought 3 packets of 10 idlis. The family ate 18. How many are left?
Leena has 5 boxes of 4 pens. She gives 2 pens to each of 3 friends. How many pens are left?
Which story fits 6 × 7?
options: 6 rows of 7 chairs. How many chairs?
quiz.explain: 6 groups of 7 is 6 × 7.
steps: 6 rows of 7 chairs is 6 groups of 7.
Answer: 6 rows of 7 chairs. How many chairs?

quiz.q: Which story fits 45 ÷ 5?
options: 45 laddoos shared by 5 friends. How many each?
quiz.explain: Sharing 45 equally among 5 is 45 ÷ 5.
steps: '45 minus 5' is subtraction, '5 boxes of 45' is multiplication.
Answer: 45 laddoos shared by 5 friends. How many each?

teach.ask: Gappu saves 3 seeds every day. How many days to save 21 seeds?
teach.nudge: How many 3s make 21?

revise.summary: Word problems use multiplication for equal groups and division for sharing equally. Some problems have two steps.
focus: Choose × or ÷ for a story.
Solve two-step problems.
Make your own story for a fact.
traps: Don't do only the first step.
Don't add or take away when the story has equal groups.
Sharing equally is division, not multiplication.

topics.title: Help Bhim: wheels, legs and horns

learn.hook: Bhim makes toy wheels. Each wheel needs 5 spokes. How many spokes for 100 wheels?
points: Each of Bhim's wheels needs 5 spokes. 10 wheels need 10 × 5 = 50 spokes.
20 wheels need 100 spokes. 100 wheels need 500 spokes.
To find how many wheels from 35 spokes: 35 ÷ 5 = 7 wheels.
Legs: a cow 4, a spider 8, an ant 6. An auto has 3 wheels. A cow has 2 horns.
Count back: 24 cow legs means 24 ÷ 4 = 6 cows.

example.q: How many spokes does Bhim need for 30 wheels?

learn.reallife: Cycle shops count spokes and wheels, and farmers count cattle by legs and horns in riddles!

quiz.q: Each wheel needs 5 spokes. How many spokes for 20 wheels?
How many spokes for 100 wheels (5 each)?
steps: Each wheel needs 5 spokes. There are 100 wheels.

quiz.q: Bhim has 40 spokes. How many wheels can he make (5 each)?
How many legs do 4 spiders have?
quiz.explain: Each spider has 8 legs. 4 × 8 = 32.
steps: Each spider has 8 legs. There are 4 spiders.

quiz.q: How many wheels do 6 autos have?
quiz.explain: An auto has 3 wheels. 6 × 3 = 18.
steps: An auto has 3 wheels. There are 6 autos.

quiz.q: A farm has cows with 28 legs in all. How many cows?
quiz.explain: Each cow has 4 legs. 28 ÷ 4 = 7.
steps: Each cow has 4 legs. 28 legs in all.

quiz.q: Some cows have 16 horns in all. How many cows?
quiz.explain: Each cow has 2 horns. 16 ÷ 2 = 8.
steps: Each cow has 2 horns. 16 horns in all.

quiz.q: How many legs do 5 ants have?
quiz.explain: An ant has 6 legs. 5 × 6 = 30.
steps: An ant has 6 legs. There are 5 ants.

teach.ask: Gappu counted 24 legs in a group of ants. How many ants are there?
teach.praise: Each ant has 6 legs, so 24 ÷ 6 = 4 ants! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How many legs does one ant have?

revise.summary: Bhim's wheels need 5 spokes each, so we multiply by 5. To go back from spokes, legs or horns to how many, we divide.
focus: Multiply to find spokes, legs or wheels.
Divide to find how many from a total.
Know legs and wheels of common things.
remember: Cow 4 legs, 2 horns. Spider 8 legs. Ant 6 legs. Auto 3 wheels.
traps: A spider has 8 legs, not 6.
An auto has 3 wheels, not 4.
Divide horns by 2, not by 4.

learn.hook: Frog Tiku jumps 7 steps each time. Can he land exactly on 50?
points: Jumping backward by 7 from 35: 28, 21, 14, 7, 0.
The largest number below 50 that Tiku lands on is 49 (7 × 7). He cannot land on 50.
A start number reaches 0 with backward jumps of 7 only if it is in the 7 table, like 21 or 42.

example.q: Tiku starts at 42 and jumps back by 7. How many jumps to reach 0?

learn.reallife: A week has 7 days, so counting weeks is counting in 7s: 7, 14, 21, 28 days.

quiz.q: Tiku jumps forward by 7 from 14. Where does he land?
Tiku jumps back by 7 from 35. Where does he land?
Starting at 0, what is the largest number below 50 that Tiku lands on?
quiz.explain: 7 × 7 = 49. The next jump is 56.

quiz.q: Which start number reaches exactly 0 with jumps of 7 back?
quiz.explain: 28 is in the 7 table: 28, 21, 14, 7, 0.
steps: A start reaches 0 only if it is in the 7 table.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number from another table

quiz.q: Which number can Tiku NOT land on, starting from 0?
quiz.explain: 40 is not in the 7 table. 35 and 42 are around it.
steps: 40 is not. It is between 35 and 42.

quiz.q: How many jumps of 7 from 0 to reach 63?
Tiku starts at 50 and jumps back by 7 again and again. Where does he stop before going below 0?
steps: From 1, a jump of 7 back goes below 0.

quiz.q: What is 6 × 7?

teach.ask: Gappu starts at 30 and hops back by 7. Will he reach 0?
teach.praise: 30, 23, 16, 9, 2... I stop at 2! 30 is not in the 7 table. Chirp!
teach.nudge: Is 30 in the table of 7?

revise.summary: Tiku jumps by 7: 7, 14, 21 ... 70. He reaches 0 going back only from numbers in the 7 table.
focus: Jump forward and back by 7.
Find how many jumps of 7 reach a number.
Tell which numbers are in the 7 table.
traps: He cannot land on 50 or 40.
Not every start reaches 0.

learn.hook: Coconut water costs ₹30 each. Four cousins want one each. Who has enough money?
points: To find the cost of many items at the same price, multiply: 4 coconuts at ₹30 each cost 4 × 30 = ₹120.
Change = money given − cost. Pay ₹200 for ₹120: change is ₹80.
A ₹500 note can be changed into smaller notes: ten ₹50 notes, or twenty-five ₹20 notes, or fifty ₹10 notes.
Mix them too: ₹500 = four ₹100 notes + two ₹50 notes.

example.q: Change ₹500 into ₹50 notes. How many notes?

learn.reallife: At a beach, you buy corn, coconut water and toys. Adding prices and getting change is everyday maths!

quiz.q: 4 coconuts cost ₹30 each. What is the total cost?
Raju pays ₹200 for things costing ₹120. How much change?
How many ₹50 notes make ₹500?
How many ₹20 notes make ₹500?
quiz.explain: ₹100 = five ₹20 notes, so ₹500 = 5 × 5 = 25 notes.

quiz.q: How many ₹10 notes make ₹500?
6 shells cost ₹5 each. Meena pays with a ₹50 note. How much change?
₹500 = four ₹100 notes + ___ ₹50 notes.
Corn costs ₹15 each. How much for 3 corns?

teach.ask: Gappu wants to buy 3 toys at ₹20 each and pay with ₹100. How much change should he get?
teach.praise: 3 × 20 = 60, and 100 − 60 = 40 change! Chirp!
teach.nudge: What is the total cost first?

revise.summary: To find the cost of many items at one price, multiply. Change is the money given minus the cost. A ₹500 note can be changed into smaller notes.
focus: Find the cost of many items.
Find the change.
Change a ₹500 note into smaller notes.
remember: ₹500 = ten ₹50 notes = twenty-five ₹20 notes = fifty ₹10 notes.
traps: Don't add the price and the number of items.
Don't forget to subtract to find change.
₹500 is ten ₹50 notes, not five.

topics.title: Sea shells and the envelope puzzle

learn.hook: 112 shells and 28 shells per necklace. How many necklaces? Keep taking away 28!
points: Division as repeated subtraction: take away 28 from 112 again and again. 112, 84, 56, 28, 0. That is 4 times.
So 112 shells make 4 necklaces of 28.
Sometimes something is left over: 100 shells, 17 per necklace: 5 necklaces use 85, and 15 are left.
The leftover (remainder) is always less than the group size.
Envelope puzzle: two numbers from 1 to 10 multiply to 24. They could be 3 and 8, or 4 and 6.

example.q: Share 23 shells equally among 5 friends.

learn.reallife: Making garlands of flowers or packing laddoos in boxes often leaves a few extra!

quiz.q: How many necklaces of 28 shells can be made from 112 shells?
100 shells, 17 per necklace. How many full necklaces?
100 shells, 17 per necklace. How many shells are left over?
26 mangoes are shared among 4 children. How many does each get and how many are left?
Can the leftover ever be equal to or more than the group size?
options: No, then one more group could be made
quiz.explain: If enough are left for another group, make it!
steps: If the leftover equals or is more than the group size, one more group can be made.
So the leftover is always less than the group size.
Answer: No, then one more group could be made

quiz.q: Two numbers from 1 to 10 multiply to 35. What are they?
steps: Both numbers must be from 1 to 10 and multiply to 35.

quiz.q: Two numbers from 1 to 10 multiply to 24. Which is NOT a correct pair?
quiz.explain: 12 is more than 10, so 2 and 12 is not allowed.

quiz.q: How many times can you take 9 away from 54?
steps: Take away 9 again and again from 54.

teach.ask: Gappu has 31 seeds to put in bags of 6. How many bags, and how many seeds are left?
teach.praise: 5 bags of 6 make 30, and 1 seed is left! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How many times can I take away 6?

revise.summary: Division can be repeated subtraction. Sometimes some are left over, and the leftover is always less than the group size.
focus: Divide by taking away again and again.
Find what is left over.
Find two numbers that multiply to a total.
remember: Two numbers from 1 to 10 that make 24: 3 and 8, or 4 and 6.
traps: Don't stop subtracting one step early.
Don't ignore the leftover.
Keep to the 1 to 10 rule in the envelope puzzle.

learn.hook: Three friends and twelve laddoos. How can everyone get the same? Let's share fairly!
points: Sharing fairly means everyone gets the same amount.
To share, give one to each person, again and again, until none are left.
12 laddoos shared by 3 friends: each friend gets 4.
Sometimes some are left over. Leftovers cannot be shared equally.
Check your sharing by multiplying: 3 friends × 4 laddoos = 12.

example.q: Kabir shares 15 marbles equally among 5 friends. How many marbles does each friend get?
steps: Give 1 marble to each friend again and again.

learn.reallife: Sharing a pack of biscuits with your cousins or dividing team players for a cricket match needs equal sharing.

games.title: Fair or not?
items: 8 apples shared by 2 children is 4 each.
Fair sharing means the oldest child gets more.
Fair means everyone gets the same amount.
9 bananas can be shared equally by 2 children with none left over.
Each gets 4 and 1 banana is left over.
16 crayons shared by 4 children is 4 each.
If 3 friends get 5 sweets each, there were 15 sweets.

quiz.q: Riya shares 12 laddoos equally among 3 friends. How many laddoos does each friend get?
quiz.explain: 12 shared into 3 equal groups gives 4 in each group. Check: 3 × 4 = 12.
steps: Give one to each friend: 3 gone
quiz.mistake: Takes away 3 from 12 instead of sharing

quiz.q: Arjun shares 10 kites equally between his 2 cousins. How many kites does each cousin get?
quiz.explain: 10 shared by 2 gives 5 each. 5 + 5 = 10.
steps: Give 1 each again and again: 5 rounds.

quiz.q: 20 rotis are shared equally by 4 people. How many rotis does each person get?
quiz.explain: 20 shared into 4 equal groups gives 5 each. Check: 4 × 5 = 20.

quiz.q: Meena shares 7 toffees equally between 2 friends. How many toffees are left over?
quiz.explain: Each friend gets 3 toffees. 3 + 3 = 6, so 7 − 6 = 1 is left over.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number each friend gets, not the leftover

quiz.q: Which is a FAIR share of 6 bananas for 2 children?
quiz.explain: Fair means the same amount. 3 and 3 are equal, and 3 + 3 = 6.

learn.hook: You may use exactly 6 paper slips. Each slip says 100, 10 or 1. What numbers can you make?
